comparison: Perfect alignment on ectopic Vg1 experiments (C4, C5, C58-C67). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing that Vg1 can induce polonaise movements independent of PS morphogenesis. OpenEval emphasizes control experiments and PIV analysis; peer reviewers highlight this as 'the most creative' approach providing convincing evidence for uncoupling.

Perfect alignment on combined mitotic arrest + ectopic Vg1 experiments (C6, C68-C73). Both evaluations support that this critical test demonstrates Vg1 can independently initiate polonaise movements. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance of mitotic arrest; peer reviewers affirm this as part of the overall uncoupling demonstration.

Strong alignment on mitotic arrest experiments (C3, C40-C57). Both evaluations support that mitosis is required for sustained but not initial polonaise movements. OpenEval covers C55-C56 (myosin cables); peer review includes C80 (model interpretation). Peer review R7 notes myosin cable analysis (C54-C56) needs further investigation for other conditions.

Strong alignment on Wnt/PCP suppression experiments (C2, C26-C39). Both evaluations support that polonaise movements persist when Wnt/PCP signaling is suppressed. OpenEval focuses on C29-C39 with statistical details; peer review additionally includes C74 and C78 (interpretive claims about PS shape effects and model implications).

Strong alignment on the overall uncoupling model (C7, C8, C81). Both evaluations support the synthesis that PS extension and polonaise movements are parallel, non-interdependent processes. OpenEval includes broader evolutionary context (C78, C80); peer review focuses on core model claims with explicit reviewer affirmation of the uncoupling conclusion.

Both identify C76 (dose-dependent Vg1 model) as uncertain/speculative. OpenEval marks it as extending beyond direct evidence; peer reviewer explicitly notes this model 'can be tested' but is not included in current study, indicating it remains untested and speculative.

Partial overlap on myosin cable analysis (C55, C56). OpenEval R2 includes these claims as part of supported mitotic arrest evidence; peer review R7 identifies myosin cable investigation as incomplete/preliminary, particularly noting it needs better investigation across all experimental conditions beyond aphidicolin treatment.

OpenEval R6 evaluates literature context and background claims (C1, C9-C25) as supported, establishing rationale for the study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/contextual claims.

OpenEval R7 identifies additional speculative/uncertain claims (C74-C75, C77, C79, C82-C83) beyond C76, including evolutionary comparisons and acknowledged gaps in understanding relationships between early and late cell flows. Peer review addresses only C76 separately and C74 within R1.

Peer review R7 identifies incomplete myosin cable analysis (C54-C56) requiring further investigation across experimental conditions. OpenEval does not separately evaluate C54 as uncertain; C55-C56 are included in R2 as part of supported mitotic arrest evidence.
